samples.question: The picture shows one narrow tape lying somewhere on a decorated board. Only the marks on the tape decide the answer; every mark off the tape is decoration and means nothing. The tape carries a black diamond at its exact middle, and one of its two ends is drawn as a solid pointed arrow tip while the other end is square. On each side of the diamond there is the same number of small coloured square marks, evenly spaced along the tape. Counting outwards from the diamond, the mark at step 1 on one side is paired with the mark at step 1 on the other side, step 2 with step 2, and so on to the last step. Every pair is made of two marks of the same colour, except for exactly one pair whose two marks have different colours. Colours repeat across pairs, and on every tape the two colours of the odd pair each occur three times in total, so counting how often a colour occurs cannot tell you which side of the diamond the answer is on. Find the one pair whose two marks differ, and look at the mark of that pair lying on the side of the diamond that has the arrow tip. What colour is it? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.
